worms.title: Remove hardware-specific categories from the dashboard
worms.description: Remove hardware-specific categories from the dashboard. We will use the hardware dashboard to track hardware issues.
worms.resolution_notes: Removed hardware categories (PCB, CAD, SIMULATION) and replaced with firmware categories in WormCategory, models, exporters, and UI templates

worms.title: Update BUG to WORM
worms.description: Update the name used for tracking issues from BUG to WORM in all code, UI and docs. Update the icon used to indicate an issue from a bug icon to a worm icon.
worms.resolution_notes: Updated issue tracking nomenclature from BUG to WORM across all data models, SQLite storage, CLI subcommands/flags, UI templates, and documentation. Replaced bug icon with worm (🪱).

worms.title: GEMINI.md should be core agent skills only
worms.description: We made a change in the hardware repo so that GEMINI.md would be for core agent skills only, and subsystem-specific skills would be moved to different files under a docs/ directory to reduce token burn. Can you locate this change in the hardware repo, and apply the same mandate here? We also need to add a back-combat mandate to firmware projects- basically, unless duly noted any firmware code should apply to all firmware targets in the repo.
worms.resolution_notes: Streamlined GEMINI.md to core agent skills, modularized subsystem guides into docs/, and added universal firmware target back-compatibility mandate.

worms.title: Change Code Review Icon to a wrench
worms.description: Change the Code Review icon used in UI from a magnifying glass icon to a wrench icon
worms.resolution_notes: Changed Code Review icon in UI from magnifying glass to wrench across diff_view and code_review templates, verified with dedicated test.

worms.title: carrier board 2.0-Create trivial "hello world" shell project
worms.description: Create a trivial "hello world" project we can use to start implementing the firmware needed for the carrier board 2.0 architecture. Create a carrier board firmware document
worms.resolution_notes: Created carrier board 2.0 shell crate with hello-world binary, tests, hardware constants, and comprehensive docs/carrier_board_firmware.md guide.

worms.title: Forgot to update the VCS UI
worms.description:
Affects commit: 330e1abbddeeedac588a5fe59eb434f28b75171b

Screenshot attached. Also, none of the WORMs are resolved

attachments.description: Pasted screenshot

worms.resolution_notes: Canonicalize commit worm tag IDs to WORM-xxx and query worms.sqlite without being overwritten by stale bugs.sqlite

worms.title: Word wrap doesn't seem to be working
worms.description: When I turn on word wrap in the dashboard tool, text still seems to be unwrapped

attachments.description: Pasted screenshot

worms.resolution_notes: Fix word wrap CSS rules for unified and side-by-side diff views in code review and diff component

worms.title: Update Contributing.md with dashboard docs
worms.resolution_notes: Added comprehensive documentation to CONTRIBUTING.md covering the System Shock 2 - Xerxes dashboard, CLI subcommands, web workstation views, SQLite and markdown synchronization, Git LFS attachments, and pre-commit invariants.

worms.title: Still seeing issues with multiple Diff Viewer windows being open after exiting from the Code Review and Bug Report windows
worms.resolution_notes: Enforced window.name reuse on Diff Viewer, Code Review, and Worm Tracker; updated returnToDashboard and setVerdict to focus opener or existing named window and close instead of spawning duplicate windows

worms.title: "Open in VSCode" didn't work
worms.description: Clicked on "Open in VSCode" next to app/carrier_board.md, and nothing seemed to happen. I was viewing the website in the VSCode simple browser window

attachments.description: Pasted text document

worms.resolution_notes: Add server /api/open-vscode endpoint and editor launcher with CLI and URL scheme fallback for embedded VS Code Simple Browser

worms.title: Feedbacks about carrier_board.md
worms.description:
Some more general feedbacks about carrier_board.md:
-host_fs should support EEPROM programming in the same way it can program other flash devices
-eeprom should be sequential storage based in a sequential format similar to USB descriptors
-the ProgramMetadata section should contain all the partition and descriptor info for a given firmware target
-we want to use FIFO for this design-cap touch, and otherwise. can we use an on chip high resolution timer to integrate and timestamp buffered samples, where needed? we also need to elaborate on how FIFO buffering will work with sensor fusion
-Production Manufacturing & Factory Provisioning- going with this approach, I think we also need some kind of structure logging and status display on the host side
-under section 6-the definition of PowerDown is diff than the one rp2040 uses; rp2040 uses these states: Active/Sleep/PowerDown. They will use the same system controller. Can we resolve this?
worms.resolution_notes: Updated app/carrier_board.md with all 6 architecture requirements: dev:eeprom host_fs support, USB-descriptor sequential-storage TLV format, ProgramMetadata partition table section, hardware FIFO and CTIMER microsecond timestamping for sensor fusion, host_cli structured logging and terminal HUD for factory provisioning, and power state harmonization with RP2040 SystemController SystemStatus (Active, Sleep, PowerDown). Added regression assertions in test_carrier_board_project.py and verified with ./tools/verify.sh.

worms.title: Dashboard stuck at 20% on launch
worms.description: Upon launching or restarting the dashboard workstation, the UI was stuck displaying the feedback database synchronization modal at 20% progress. Inspection revealed a JavaScript `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'` in `diff_view.html.j2:1705` within the `sanitizeAuthor()` function introduced during privacy sanitization hardening. Because the script failed to parse, `initDiffView()` and `performInitialSync()` never ran, leaving the modal stuck at its initial 20% HTML state.
worms.resolution_notes:
1. Pruned dangling closing parenthesis in `sanitizeAuthor()` condition in `tools/dashboard/templates/diff_view.html.j2`.
2. Hardened workstation initialization lifecycle so `initDiffView()` fires immediately if `document.readyState !== 'loading'`, eliminating dependency on potentially pre-fired `DOMContentLoaded` events.
3. Added comprehensive regression test `test_regression_bug_translucent_tapeworm_953_dashboard_js_syntax_and_sync_screen` in `tools/tests/test_dashboard.py` verifying balanced syntax and executing `node -c` across extracted `<script>` blocks in all dashboard templates (`diff_view.html.j2`, `code_review.html.j2`, `worm_report.html.j2`).

worms.title: Elide physical address and personal email in privacy sanitizer
worms.description: Extend the zero-dependency personal privacy and identity sanitizer (`tools/dashboard/provider/sanitizer.py`) to systematically redact physical addresses (street names, numbers, suite/apt/unit designators, P.O. Boxes, and postal/ZIP codes) and personal email addresses (user handles, consumer email domains like `@gmail.com`, `@me.com`, etc.) across developer feedback, bug reports, and logs. Additionally, update VCS engine commit author and email mapping to redact user author identities to `User` and `user@workspace`.
worms.resolution_notes:
1. Added physical street address, unit/suite, and P.O. Box regex redaction to `<address>` and `<zip>` in `elide_personal_info()`, using pure regex matching without requiring an engineering whitelist or supplier address preservation.

worms.description: TMC6300 3-phase BLDC driver requires 6 independent PWM/GPIO inputs (UH, UL, VH, VL, WH, WL) for proper 3-phase commutation. Added dedicated unit tests and regression assertions guarding against shoot-through and ensuring independent low-side conduction.

worms.title: Motor does not spin
worms.description: Motor does not spin, current readings are constant at 7 mA. See tracebacks below
worms.expected_behavior: During motor operation, the 6-PWM bridge outputs continuous 25 kHz PWM switching across commutating phase pairs (U, V, W) at the proper electrical commutation angle (6-step trapezoidal commutation) to generate a rotating stator magnetic field. When commanded to speed 100%, the driver continuously energizes the phases according to the rotating commutation sequence.
worms.actual_behavior: In the attached logic analyzer capture (`digital.csv`), when commanded to `motor speed 100`, only Phase U High (`UH`) and Phase V Low (`VL`) exhibit activity, pulsing briefly for 2.88 to 40 microseconds on each 10 ms (100 Hz) `motor_controller` tick. Phases UL, VH, WL, and WH remain completely unasserted (logic 0.0V) across the entire capture. The commutation sequence never advances beyond initial step 0 (`UH=1, VL=1`), failing to generate a rotating stator magnetic field, which leaves the motor stationary. Consequently, motor current consumption remains flat at standby (7 mA), and upon expiration of the 3-second startup blanking window, the controller triggers a low load / dry detection fault and halts the motor.

custom_sections.title: Trace Analysis (`digital.csv`)
custom_sections.content:
1. **Pulse Timing & Periodicity**:
   - Pulses occur at exact ~10.0 ms intervals (e.g., $t=15.143874$, $15.153815$, $15.163800$, $15.173784$, etc.), which precisely corresponds to the 100 Hz tick rate of `motor_controller::tick_motor`.
   - Each pulse duration spans only 2.88 µs to ~40 µs before instantly returning all outputs to zero. Continuous 25 kHz PWM modulation is absent between ticks.
2. **Channel Distribution**:
   - Channel 2 (`UH`) and Channel 3 (`VL`) toggle together on every 10 ms pulse (`0,1,1,0,0,0`).
   - Channel 1 (`UL`), Channel 4 (`VH`), Channel 5 (`WL`), and Channel 6 (`WH`) remain constant 0.
   - Initial commutation step 0 uses mask `0b001001` (UH=1, VL=1). The lack of commutation advance indicates either the state machine word recycling drops on non-blocking pull, or `commutation_step` is continually reset or overridden before phase progression can occur.
3. **Current & Fault Telemetry Correlation**:
   - Standby current: 7 mA (measured by INA219).
   - Startup blanking duration: 3.0 seconds (300 ticks). At $t \approx 3.2$ s after start command, `update()` flags `Low load / dry detected (current: 7 mA)` and stops the motor.
4. **Status**:
   - Issue remains **OPEN** per user direction pending definitive hardware/gate-driver bench validation and commutation sequencer root-cause resolution.

worms.resolution_notes: Decoupled set_speed from sm.tx push in Tmc6300Pio, ensuring tick exclusively drives 6-step trapezoidal commutation advancement and non-blocking 25 kHz PIO PWM word recycling without FIFO overflow.

worms.title: Parse ANSI OSC 8 hyperlink escape sequences in terminal and CLI console
worms.description: Cargo and CLI utilities emit ANSI OSC 8 hyperlink sequences (\x1b]8;;<url>\x1b\ or \x1b]8;;<url>\x07). Terminal formatters in dashboard and host_daemon do not recognize OSC 8 escapes, causing raw '8;;https://...' text to be rendered in the CLI console.
worms.resolution_notes: Parsed ANSI OSC 8 hyperlink escape sequences (\x1b]8;;url\x1b\text\x1b]8;;\x1b\ as well as BEL-terminated and orphaned 8;; sequences) into styled HTML anchor tags across terminal.py, code_review.html.j2, and host_daemon.html.j2, preventing raw '8;;' from rendering in the CLI console.

worms.title: VL not asserting
worms.description: The PIO program is not asserting VL. This is causing an overcurrent condition which asserts the DIAG pin. See attached trace

attachments.description: Uploaded document digital.csv

worms.resolution_notes: Corrected TMC6300 pin mapping and 6-step trapezoidal commutation masks to match physical SparkFun TMC6300 J1 header pinout (UL, UH, VL, VH, WL, WH mapped to GP16..GP21). VL (bit 2 / GP18) now properly asserts in steps 0 and 5.

custom_sections.title: Waveform Analysis & Scope Comparison
custom_sections.content:
![TMC6300 Commutation Waveform Comparison](../recordings/previews/waveform_gliding_larva_522.svg)

##### 1. Observed Output Waveform (`attachments/WORM-GLIDING-LARVA-522/digital.csv`)
- **Step 0 ($t = 0.00\,\text{ms} \to 10.00\,\text{ms}$)**: Firmware energized **UL** (GP17) and **WH** (GP20).
- **Step 1 ($t = 10.00\,\text{ms} \to 19.89\,\text{ms}$)**: Firmware energized **VL** (GP19) and **WH** (GP20).
- **Fault ($t \approx 20\,\text{ms}$)**: High-side driver held WH continuously across both steps while switching low sides in reverse polarity. The resultant reverse magnetic stator flux locked the rotor against permanent magnets, driving coil current into saturation and asserting the hardware `DIAG` fault pin (GP22). The motor controller caught the fault, transitioned state to `MotorState::Off`, and de-energized all gates.

##### 2. Expected Canonical Waveform (6-Step Trapezoidal BLDC)
- **Step 0 ($t = 0 \to 10\,\text{ms}$)**: **UH** (GP16) & **VL** (GP19) active; Phase W floating.
- **Step 1 ($t = 10 \to 20\,\text{ms}$)**: **UH** (GP16) & **WL** (GP21) active; Phase V floating.
- **Step 2 ($t = 20 \to 30\,\text{ms}$)**: **VH** (GP18) & **WL** (GP21) active; Phase U floating.
- **Step 3 ($t = 30 \to 40\,\text{ms}$)**: **VH** (GP18) & **UL** (GP17) active; Phase W floating.
- **Step 4 ($t = 40 \to 50\,\text{ms}$)**: **WH** (GP20) & **UL** (GP17) active; Phase V floating.
- **Step 5 ($t = 50 \to 60\,\text{ms}$)**: **WH** (GP20) & **VL** (GP19) active; Phase U floating.
- **DIAG (GP22)**: Remains low throughout operation; motor accelerates smoothly with continuous commutation.

worms.resolution_notes: Root cause identified: Inverted TMC6300 pin mapping and phase masks from commit 1a7ef379 caused firmware to energize UL and WH in Step 0 and VL and WH in Step 1, creating reverse magnetic fields that locked the rotor, causing stall overcurrent and tripping TMC6300 DIAG fault pin at t = 20 ms. Restored canonical pin assignments (UH=16, UL=17, VH=18, VL=19, WH=20, WL=21) and canonical 6-step trapezoidal commutation masks across board, peripheral driver, and codegen. Added waveform comparison preview under recordings/previews/waveform_gliding_larva_522.svg and codified regression unit tests in peripheral/tests/integration.rs and tools/tests/test_worm_gliding_larva_522_commutation_phase_progression.py.

worms.title: TMC6300-Short protection fault on startup
worms.description: The short protection circuit of the TMC6300 motor driver will prevent motor communication and assert the DIAG pin if it detects a short between any FET for more than 1 uS in order to prevent overheating. The winding resistance of the motor is 0.5 Ohm; so we must make sure to connect each winding for less than 1 uS (ideally 0.5us to 0.8us) in order to commutate the motor. We have previously (in another session) verified power is good with a battery connected during motor startup, so this was the next thing we needed to invesgitate and fix with the motor driver.
reproduction_steps: 1. $ PROBE_RS_SPEED=4000 cargo run --target thumbv6m-none-eabi --package cat_detector --bin cat_detector_shell —release
2. motor speed 10

attachments.description: Uploaded document digital.csv
Pasted screenshot screenshot_paste_1792623504516_fkls0.png

worms.resolution_notes: Configured TMC6300 PIO clock divider to 5 (25 MHz) and clamped active duty cycle on-count to 7..=14 cycles, ensuring commutation winding connection pulses strictly stay between 520 ns and 800 ns (< 1.0 us t_S2G short protection delay) across all motor speeds to eliminate short-circuit trips on startup.

worms.description: When host.py is invoked without arguments, confirming the target package configuration modal displays the flashing matrix modal (syncModal) but fails to initiate progress polling (startSyncPolling), leaving the UI permanently frozen at 0% with "Synchronizing target firmware...". Furthermore, invoking host.py with no arguments while a daemon is running with different build profile flags erroneously treats default CLI options as a configuration change and starts background sync without bringing forward the UI.
worms.resolution_notes: Fixed submitTargetConfig in host_daemon.html.j2 to trigger startSyncPolling() and initialize UI progress indicators. Synchronously set active state in runner.sync_async() to avoid polling race conditions. Guarded config_changed in cli.py with is_explicit so invoking host.py with no args against a running daemon preserves configuration.

worms.title: Motor vibrates, does not spin & 92 mA current cap
worms.description: The motor vibrates and only pulls ~92-94 mA at 100% commanded speed. The motor RPM is reported as 0, and the motor only vibrates rather than spinning even when running freely unloaded.

custom_sections.title: Root Cause Analysis
custom_sections.content:
1. **92 mA Current Cap & 14% Duty Cycle Clamp**:
   In `peripheral/src/tmc6300.rs`, `clamp_on_count_short_protection` clamped the PIO duty cycle `on_count` to `SHORT_PROTECTION_MAX_ON_COUNT = 14` out of 100 cycles ($4\,\mu\text{s}$ at 250 kHz). Consequently, the effective PWM duty cycle was clamped to ~14% even when commanded to 100%, causing the ~92 mA current draw and lack of torque to overcome detent/cogging torque and fluid friction.
2. **Frequency Modulation Solution**:
   To deliver full torque without violating the TMC6300 $t_{\text{S2G}} = 1.0\,\mu\text{s}$ short-circuit delay, implemented `calculate_pwm_counts`:
   - For $D \le 14\%$: fixed 100-cycle period ($4\,\mu\text{s}$), $T_{\text{on}} = D$, $T_{\text{off}} = 100 - D$.
   - For $D > 14\%$: hold $T_{\text{on}} = 14$ cycles ($800\,\text{ns} < 1.0\,\mu\text{s}$) and modulate $T_{\text{off}}$ downward to 1 cycle.
   - At $D = 100\%$: $T_{\text{on}} = 14, T_{\text{off}} = 1$, yielding ~93.3% duty cycle with a 160 ns de-energization window that resets the driver short-circuit comparator on every pulse without tripping DIAG.
3. **Motor Configuration Architecture**:
   Decoupled motor controller parameters into a dedicated `MotorConfig` struct in `model::types` and configured `[boards.cat_detector.motor]` in `board.toml` with code generation support, resolving code review finding `f6f27e52`.

worms.resolution_notes: Resolved 92 mA current draw cap by implementing frequency-modulated duty cycle scaling in calculate_pwm_counts, delivering ~93.3% effective duty cycle up to 1.57A current while strictly constraining FET conduction pulses to <= 800 ns (< 1.0 us t_S2G). Power-cycled hardware to clear latched DIAG fault and verified motor draws 356 mA at speed 50 and 1572 mA at speed 100 with GP22 remaining 0.

worms.title: Host flashes cat_detector_app instead of shell due to session contamination
worms.description: When flashing or running host daemon without explicit target arguments, cat_detector_app gets flashed instead of cat_detector_shell. Root cause: test_worm_composted_palolo_725 overwrites target/host_session.json with cat_detector_app during pytest runs, discover_target_packages defaults to first binary in Cargo.toml, and app/Cargo.toml lacks default-run.
worms.resolution_notes: Configured default-run = 'cat_detector_shell' and prioritized shell binaries in target discovery. Isolated test sessions with tmp_path and guarded save_last_session against PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST to prevent test suites from polluting the developer's live workspace host session.

worms.title: Motor oscillates at speed 30
worms.description:
Some additional context here:

  ### Remediation Plan

  1. **Torque Floor & Duty Scaling in calculate_pwm_counts**:
      • Modulate OFF-count within a window that sustains sufficient inductive current to overcome physical cogging detents (> 150 mA)
      while preserving individual FET ON-pulse clamping (t_{ON} ≤ 800 ns) so the TMC6300 t_{S2G} comparator never trips.
  2. **Commutation Step Scaling & Soft-Start Ramp in MotorController**:
      • Align calculate_commutation_step_ticks and the soft-start acceleration ramp so the motor starts reliably and scales smoothly into
      continuous rotation without pole slipping.
  3. Hardware Verification:
      • Re-flash target via python tools/host.py sync and confirm smooth rotation at speeds 10, 30, 50, and 100 via interactive CLI.

  ### 3. Core 1 Concurrency Risks at 500 μs Ticks & Mitigations

  Core 1 executes the following tasks under Embassy's cooperative executor:
  • controllers.core1.motor (MotorController)
  • controllers.core1.sensor_north, sensor_east, sensor_west (VL53L0X ToF distance sensors)
  • core1_command_task (command routing from Core 0)
  • core_monitor (MPU stack guard & watchdog)

   Potential Risk                  | Root Cause Mechanism                             | Verified Mitigation in Codebase
  ---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------
   I2C Bus Contention & Starvation | INA219 and the 3 VL53L0X distance sensors share  | Fast tick is 100% I2C-free: The 500 μs
                                   | SHARED_I2C via mutex. An I2C transaction takes   | commutation tick tick_motor() only pushes a 32-
                                   | 100--400 μs. If MotorController polled I2C every | bit word to the PIO TX FIFO and samples the GPIO
                                   | 500 μs, the distance sensors would starve and    | pin. Execution takes < 50 CPU cycles (≈ 350 ns,
                                   | the motor tick deadline would overrun.           | or 0.07% CPU load). All I2C current reads and
                                   |                                                  | safety limit checks are strictly quarantined to
                                   |                                                  | the 1.0-second slow telemetry tick
                                   |                                                  | (MOTOR_INACTIVE_TICK_INTERVAL).
   Cooperative Executor Starvation | Tasks only yield at .await points. If the motor  | Bounded non-blocking channel drain + explicit
                                   | task looped or blocked, other Core 1 tasks would | .await yield: The active loop drains pending
                                   | hang.                                            | commands non-blockingly via while let Ok(cmd) =
                                   |                                                  | command_rx.try_receive() (bounded to channel
                                   |                                                  | capacity 4), executes tick_motor(), and
                                   |                                                  | immediately yields to the executor via
                                   |                                                  | ticker.next().await.
   Idle CPU Burn                   | Running a 500 μs ticker when the motor is        | Dynamic Ticker Lifecycle: When stopped, the 500
                                   | stopped would waste CPU cycles and battery       | μs ticker is dropped. MotorController waits on
                                   | power.                                           | command_rx.receive() with a 1.0-second timeout,
                                   |                                                  | consuming 0 CPU cycles when idle.

worms.resolution_notes: 1. Fixed TMC6300 PIO assembler to shift exactly 6 bits to OUT pins followed by 2 null bits, preventing RP2040 out_count modulo wrapping from overwriting GP16 (UH) and GP17 (UL) with zeros and deadlocking Phase U. 2. Scaled open-loop startup commutation interval to 60 ticks (30ms) for smooth open-loop acceleration without rotor pole-slipping. 3. Preserved commutation step interval and state across running speed changes in motor_controller. 4. Added regression tests in controller_tests and integration.rs. 5. Redacted personal paths in system log attachments.

worms.title: Regression tests are not useful
worms.description: I noticed some regression tests are silly and not useful, and only wrap other test cases. If a test case that a bug is meant to fix does not check for the bug, can we instead update the original test case directly if possible? If not possible to unit test a regression fix, it is preferable to omit a regression test if it does not do anything new. Can we please remove these types of useless regression tests in both hardware and firmware repos, as well as update learnings about regression test best practices.

worms.resolution_notes: Resolved thermal DIAG tripping during extended ramp stress tests. Tightened closed-loop current regulation to regulate within 450..=550 mA (nominal 500 mA) with CLOSED_LOOP_REGULATION_CEILING_MA = 550. When current exceeds 550 mA under load, duty cycle is actively throttled down by 5% per cycle, preventing sustained ~760 mA coil current and keeping driver temperature well below the 150°C thermal shutdown threshold.

worms.resolution_notes: Resolved standstill pole-slip stall when starting motor at 50% speed. Configured startup_commutation_step_ticks = 100 in board.toml, ensuring that regardless of commanded speed, initial motor breakaway begins at 100 ticks (33.3 ms per step = 50 RPM) so the stationary rotor locks to the stator field, after which the soft-start ramp smoothly accelerates to target speed (4 ticks = 1,250 RPM). Verified on live target hardware with 50% start passing cleanly without stall.

worms.title: Only first commit in smartlog tree gets highlighted
worms.description: In diff_view.html.j2, selectCommit attempts to find active commit elements via document.getElementById('node-' + commitHash.slice(0, 7)). When git abbreviations exceed 7 characters (e.g. 8-char short SHAs), element lookup returns null, causing commit selection highlights to fail on click.
worms.resolution_notes: Fixed selectCommit in diff_view.html.j2 across firmware and hardware repositories. Replaced fragile slice(0, 7) element lookups with event.currentTarget and data-hash attribute matching (exact and prefix), supporting arbitrary-length git abbreviated hashes (e.g. 8-char SHAs). Added data-hash='working' to working tree node and updated dynamic renderSmartlogList to preserve active class across selection transitions. Added dedicated regression unit tests in tools/tests/test_worm_creeping_tapeworm_215_smartlog_highlight.py and hardware tests.
